name: AI Engineer Core
description: Core preparation for engineers building LLM-powered applications: LLM fundamentals, prompting, RAG, retrieval, evaluation, safety, and operations.

studyPlan.name: Choose the smallest useful AI approach
studyPlan.exercise: Take a support-answering feature. Write the simplest non-LLM baseline, then choose prompting, retrieval or fine-tuning. Specify the evidence that would change your choice.
readinessChecks: Explain token and context limits without confusing them with factual knowledge.
Defend the choice using freshness, quality, privacy and ongoing cost rather than model popularity.

studyPlan.name: Make output measurable and testable
studyPlan.exercise: Build a ten-case evaluation fixture including malformed output, unanswerable requests and conflicting evidence. Separate retrieval failures from generation failures. Add one regression assertion before proposing a fix.
readinessChecks: Validate model output before it reaches a side-effecting system.
Show a failing case and explain which measurement identifies the failing component.

studyPlan.name: Defend a production release
studyPlan.exercise: Give a 30-minute design walkthrough and reserve ten minutes for objections. Cover permissions, capacity, evaluation gates, failure handling and rollback; then explain how your design changes at ten times the traffic.
readinessChecks: State a measurable quality floor and latency/cost budget.
Name a credible injection failure and a release-blocking test, not just a safety prompt.

name: RAG & Azure AI Specialist
description: Focused preparation for building grounded AI systems with Azure AI Search, Document Intelligence, embeddings, citations, and production RAG patterns.

studyPlan.name: Model the corpus and retrieval problem
studyPlan.exercise: Sketch an index for policies with document version, tenant, access group and effective date. Compare two chunking approaches on the same three documents and state what you would measure.
readinessChecks: Explain why chunk size and embedding choice need task-specific evaluation.
Keep access filtering and document freshness explicit in the retrieval contract.

studyPlan.name: Implement and diagnose retrieval
studyPlan.exercise: Calculate reciprocal-rank fusion for two short ranked lists. Then investigate a recall drop after reindexing with a frozen query set, checking filters, embeddings and index configuration one variable at a time.
readinessChecks: Distinguish recall, ranking quality and answer faithfulness.
Propose a discriminating experiment and a rollback criterion before changing the model.

studyPlan.name: Defend tenant-safe production RAG
studyPlan.exercise: Whiteboard a multi-tenant retrieval service. Trace a request through authorization, retrieval, generation and logging. Inject a stale permission and an unavailable search service, then describe containment and recovery.
readinessChecks: Enforce authorization independently of generated text and include negative cross-tenant tests.
Explain degradation, index migration and cost/latency trade-offs at higher load.

name: Agentic AI Engineer
description: Preparation for tool-using agents, agent frameworks, orchestration, planning, memory, evaluation, and operational safeguards.

studyPlan.name: Choose orchestration deliberately
studyPlan.exercise: Compare a deterministic workflow, a single tool-using agent and a multi-agent design for the same approval task. Draw where state lives and where human authority is required.
readinessChecks: Explain what an agent framework and MCP each provide without treating either as an authorization boundary.
Justify additional agents with measurable benefits over a simpler baseline.

studyPlan.name: Bound tool execution
studyPlan.exercise: Write pseudocode for a bounded tool loop with schema validation, per-tool authorization, timeouts, a step budget and an idempotency key for writes. Test a repeated call, invalid arguments and an injected instruction.
readinessChecks: Keep permissions outside model control and require approval for consequential actions.
Explain cancellation, retry safety and a visible failure state when a budget is exhausted.

studyPlan.name: Evaluate the entire workflow
studyPlan.exercise: Defend a procurement-agent design under a tool outage and partial completion. Define five end-to-end test cases, intermediate trace checks, cost limits and a human handoff with enough context to continue safely.
readinessChecks: Measure task success, tool correctness and policy adherence separately.
Describe durable state, recovery and failure isolation rather than assuming each step succeeds.

name: Azure Integration Engineer
description: Preparation for Azure API Management, Functions, Logic Apps, messaging, observability, security, migration, and service integration.

studyPlan.name: Establish integration contracts
studyPlan.exercise: Trace an incoming order from API to background processing. Choose request/response, a work queue or an event stream for each boundary and specify ownership of authentication, validation and retries.
readinessChecks: Distinguish commands from events and justify delivery semantics.
Avoid treating an API gateway as a substitute for backend authorization.

studyPlan.name: Diagnose the whole request path
studyPlan.exercise: Investigate an intermittent timeout using a trace spanning gateway, compute and database. Rank three hypotheses, name the metric that separates them and define a safe mitigation. Compare code and workflow-based integration ownership.
readinessChecks: Differentiate queueing, connection exhaustion and downstream latency.
Explain which action reduces impact without hiding the underlying error.

studyPlan.name: Make recovery part of the design
studyPlan.exercise: Design order processing with human approval. Walk through a crash after a database commit but before publishing, a duplicate message and a poison message. Include reconciliation, replay and observability.
readinessChecks: Explain outbox and idempotent consumption without promising exactly-once side effects.
Account for backpressure, failure recovery and scaling bottlenecks.

name: .NET Cloud Engineer
description: Preparation for C#, ASP.NET Core, cloud-native .NET services, integration, architecture, resilience, and Azure platform patterns.

studyPlan.name: Reason about request lifetimes
studyPlan.exercise: Trace one HTTP request through middleware and a scoped service into asynchronous I/O. Identify where cancellation flows and explain why a singleton must not capture request-scoped state.
readinessChecks: Explain await without claiming it always creates a thread.
Predict a lifetime or middleware-ordering bug before running the code.

studyPlan.name: Code and diagnose data access
studyPlan.exercise: Implement the order aggregation with tests for empty input, time boundaries and ties. Inspect generated SQL or query counts, then diagnose repeated enumeration and excess materialization with a before/after measurement.
readinessChecks: State when the query executes and what runs in the database versus memory.
Use profiling evidence rather than adding caching before locating the bottleneck.

studyPlan.name: Defend a resilient cloud service
studyPlan.exercise: Design a multi-tenant catalog API. Specify access checks, indexing, capacity, cancellation and downstream resilience. Inject a retry storm and a noisy tenant and explain which limit contains each.
readinessChecks: Make retries bounded and safe for writes.
Explain isolation and cache invalidation alongside latency and scaling trade-offs.

name: Java Cloud Engineer
description: Preparation for Java, Spring Boot, cloud-native backend services, migration, integration, architecture, and Azure platform patterns.

studyPlan.name: Explain runtime and dependency behavior
studyPlan.exercise: Trace an order request through a Spring service. Explain object lifetime, contention and memory growth, then compare a lock-based update with an atomic operation for a narrowly defined invariant.
readinessChecks: Separate heap pressure, stack exhaustion and thread contention.
Explain dependency injection and concurrency guarantees without relying on annotations as magic.

studyPlan.name: Measure query and concurrency failures
studyPlan.exercise: Implement and test order aggregation. Capture SQL query counts for an endpoint, fix an N+1 pattern and verify pagination still works. Outline how you would distinguish a database bottleneck from GC or thread-pool pressure.
readinessChecks: Demonstrate a measurable reduction in queries without loading an unbounded graph.
Use traces, pool metrics and GC evidence to eliminate competing hypotheses.

studyPlan.name: Design migration and delivery safety
studyPlan.exercise: Plan a strangler migration for order processing. Define the routing boundary, data ownership, outbox, replay and rollback. Explain how the system behaves when old and new versions coexist.
readinessChecks: Avoid unsafe dual writes and specify reconciliation.
Tie migration phases to business continuity, compatibility checks and operational ownership.

name: Python AI Application Engineer
description: Preparation for Python, FastAPI, async services, Azure Functions, RAG applications, Azure AI integration, and production AI app patterns.

studyPlan.name: Choose concurrency and streaming boundaries
studyPlan.exercise: Build a typed generator pipeline over synthetic rows. Explain where memory remains bounded and choose an execution model separately for network I/O and CPU-heavy work, stating interpreter assumptions.
readinessChecks: Distinguish concurrency from parallel execution and state version-specific assumptions.
Handle malformed rows and resource cleanup without loading the entire input.

studyPlan.name: Keep an async service responsive
studyPlan.exercise: Write tests exposing shared mutable defaults. For a streaming endpoint, simulate a slow dependency, a disconnected client and CPU-heavy processing. Explain bounded concurrency, cancellation and backpressure.
readinessChecks: Remove event-loop blocking using an execution model appropriate to the workload.
Verify timeout and cleanup behavior, not only the successful response.

studyPlan.name: Operate an authenticated AI service
studyPlan.exercise: Design a Python RAG service from ingestion to response. Trace workload identity and tenant access, set quality/latency budgets and investigate a sudden hallucination increase using a frozen evaluation set.
readinessChecks: Separate infrastructure identity from end-user authorization.
Locate the failing pipeline stage before changing a prompt or model.

name: Engineering Manager (AI/Cloud)
description: IC→manager and seasoned-manager prep: people, hiring, performance, conflict, prioritization, org design, and behavioral/STAR for AI/cloud teams.

studyPlan.name: Define your management operating model
studyPlan.exercise: Prepare a two-minute explanation of why management fits your experience. Draft a hiring rubric and a technical-debt decision with explicit business impact, then identify what evidence would change the decision.
readinessChecks: Use real examples and separate your actions from the team's work.
Describe consistent hiring evidence rather than intuition or culture-fit shorthand.

studyPlan.name: Rehearse difficult conversations
studyPlan.exercise: Role-play a conflict and a prioritization disagreement. Prepare a one-minute and a three-minute failure story with your mistake, stakeholder response, measurable outcome and what you changed afterward.
readinessChecks: Show listening, clear expectations and follow-through without blaming individuals.
Distinguish a real result from a hypothetical improvement; do not invent metrics.

studyPlan.name: Defend delivery and organizational choices
studyPlan.exercise: Present a team design and recovery plan for an at-risk AI launch. Allocate owners, reduce scope, state safety gates and explain the escalation and communication plan to a skeptical product partner.
readinessChecks: Connect staffing and sequencing to dependencies, capacity and customer impact.
Explain a principled stop/go decision and how the team learns without punishment.

name: Staff+ IC (Principal / Architect)
description: Staff, Principal, Distinguished IC and Architect prep: technical strategy, scope, influence-without-authority, architecture review, AI org strategy.

studyPlan.name: Show scope and technical judgment
studyPlan.exercise: Prepare a one-page technical strategy: problem, constraints, alternatives, recommendation, staged adoption and success measures. Annotate the decisions you owned and the decisions delegated to others.
readinessChecks: Connect architecture choices to business outcomes and explicit assumptions.
Explain what would invalidate the strategy and which decisions are reversible.

studyPlan.name: Demonstrate influence and multiplication
studyPlan.exercise: Rehearse a resisted technical change, a mentorship outcome and a disagreement. Identify stakeholders, incentives, the pilot, adoption evidence and how you reduced dependence on yourself.
readinessChecks: Demonstrate influence without borrowing authority from title or reporting lines.
Show lasting team capability and acknowledge counterarguments and mistakes.

studyPlan.name: Lead an architecture and strategy review
studyPlan.exercise: Run a review for an AI capability with strict availability and residency constraints. State assumptions, failure domains, RTO/RPO, cost and staged rollout. Challenge active-active complexity and defend a simpler alternative.
readinessChecks: Quantify recovery objectives and expose consistency or residency conflicts.
Include organizational ownership, evaluation gates and an exit strategy, not only a component diagram.
